To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the TP clearance can be estimated from creatinine clearance and (2) the TP clearance and volume of distribution can be predicted with high accuracy from two or three TP plasma concentrations using the Bayesian approach.
TP clearance was highly correlated with CrCL and TP pharmacokinetic parameter can be estimated using only 3 plasma concentration measurement and the Bayesian approach.

(1) the clearance of carboplatin total platinum is highly correlated to the clearance of creatinine; (2) this relationship, together with the morphological and biological characteristics of the patient, can be used to estimate carboplatin total plasma platinum clearance; (3) this method of individualisation is as reliable as the Bayesian approach; (4) this method is more reliable than the individualisation based on the clearance of ultrafiltered platinum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a model for individualised dosing of carboplatin, which takes into account the pharmacokinetic variability of the drug.
the development of a new model for the estimation of carboplatin pharmacokinetics.
the pharmacokinetic modelling of carboplatin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
carboplatin clearance may be reliably estimated using the Cockroft and Gaull equation and that this approach is more reliable than using ultrafiltered platinum.
the estimation of TP pharmacokinetcs is reliable and may be used in clinical practice.
TP is a more reliable parameter for carboplatin dosing than UP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of TP is a more reliable method for the determination of the pharmacokinetic parameters than the UP.
the use of the Cockroft and Gaul method, together with only the morphological and biological data, is a simple and reliable method to estimate TP pharmacokinetic data.
the Bayesian approach is the most accurate method for carboplatin dose adjustment, followed by the Cockroft and Gaull method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the Bayesian approach can be used in the clinic to estimate the pharmacokinetic parameters for carboplatin, and that this method can be used in clinical practice.
the use of TP instead of UP for carboplatin dose individualisation may improve the accuracy of dose estimation.
the use of a Bayesian method to predict carboplatin pharmacokinetics in cancer patients is feasible and reliable.
